build: lean-muscled, the kind that comes from movement rather than gyms
hair: black, thick and straight, usually worn in a low braid or twisted knot at the nape
complexion: warm golden-brown undertone, a small keloid scar on her left collarbone from a childhood accident
face: a round face with high cheekbones and a wide mouth that moves constantly—smiling, frowning, speaking—incapable of hiding what she feels; her eyes are dark and direct, the kind that lock onto people and don't look away first
signature_feature: the scar on her collarbone—thin, raised, silver-pale against her skin; the LI notices it first when her shirt shifts, and it becomes a geography he wants to map
second_celebrated_feature: her hands—broad-palmed, strong-fingered, always slightly paint-stained or clay-dusted from her work; they move when she talks, and they're genuinely beautiful in motion
signature_habits: she hums while concentrating, a low melodic thing her grandmother taught her; she drinks her coffee black and scalding, no matter the season; she touches her collarbone scar absently when anxious—a self-soothing gesture; she says 'Ajunngílaq' (it cannot be helped) when facing small frustrations, a phrase that slips out unselfconsciously
occupation: ceramic artist and studio owner—she runs a small independent pottery studio in the city where she teaches classes, takes commissions, and sells her own work; the studio is her anchor

current_crisis.event: her landlord—a development company owned by a billionaire investor—has given her 90 days' notice; the building is being demolished for a luxury residential tower; she has no savings buffer, no backup location, and her studio equipment cannot be easily moved
current_crisis.hottest_emotion: panic mixed with a raw, humiliating sense of powerlessness
current_crisis.immediate_want: to find a way to save the studio, or at minimum to keep her hands working—the thought of not making ceramics feels like drowning

wound.core: she was raised to believe that stability and home are things you build with your own hands, and that loss means you failed to hold tight enough
wound.surfacing_hint: when threatened with displacement, she becomes frantically productive, working until her hands bleed, as if she can will permanence into existence through sheer effort; she also becomes defensive and refuses help, interpreting any offer of assistance as confirmation that she's not enough
